body_html:
Most advice on this topic is vague. This guide is a field note: what to change on your site this week so you stand out for the right reasons.

Recruiters and clients don’t owe you a deep read. If the first screen is confusing, they leave.

This guide is for builders polishing the details that change first impressions who want a site that feels intentional — not another generic template dump.

The real problem

Smart portfolios feel calm: one idea per section, outcomes before tools, and a next step that doesn’t beg.

Do this next

  1. Delete anything you can’t defend in an interview
  2. Test on a phone before you share
  3. Ask one mentor for a 60-second reaction

PDF + site, not PDF or site

Keep the PDF for portals that demand uploads. Use the live site for humans. Put the URL in the resume header so both assets point to each other.

Tools vs presentation

Free builders are fine for drafts. When the link goes on a CV, presentation quality becomes part of your professional signal — templates exist so you skip reinventing layout.

How a website helps you stand out

Small craft decisions — photo quality, copy length, load speed — compound into “this person seems sharp.”

On BEXO, that path is simple: discover on mybexo.com, create on dash.mybexo.com, share on yourname.atbexo.com. Premium templates and a Hire Me page give you agency-grade presentation without becoming a full-time webmaster.

Field checklist

  • Delete anything you can’t defend in an interview
  • Test on a phone before you share
  • Ask one mentor for a 60-second reaction

Try this today

Open your draft (or start one), apply one change from the list above, and publish. Momentum compounds faster than waiting for “ready.”
